main_text.p: bem diffunditis. Quare & ego impul-sus sum, vt laesam veltrā Pietatem, mo-destâ quadam defensione placandā ex-istimārim.] Augusta quidē haec de Cae-sarea Potestate, magnificentius tamē il-lud & ad praesens propositum accōmo-datius,ejusdem B.Cyrilli in Principio li-bri sui de recta in Christi fide ad Theodosi-um Imperatorem nuncupati : [Vt sum-mo illi numini, omne genu incuruatur, Thronique, Dominationes, Principa-tus, ac Potestates prona submittentes colla, congruis illud laudibꝰ ac hymnis venerantur : ita in vestrâ quoq; sereni-tate apprimè conspicua & gloriosa, ve-nustam quandam summae illius gloriae imaginem intueri licet; vos etiam om-ni terreno fastigio superioris amplissi-marum dignitatum fontes estis,vos hu-manae felicitatis principia&origines.] Cyrillo suffragatur eius In 13.ad Rom. συνχρονας [?] § Theo-doretus: [cum vult, inquit, eos qui pec-cant, castigare, eos etiam à malis Ma-gistratibus regi permittit. Dabo enim adolescetulos Principes eorum, & illu-sores dominabuntur eis.Concludā hoc caput, cum illo Prosperi {h} Epigrammate.h 34.

page.notes: The Greek word after "eius" is printed unclearly and is given with [?]; the sign before "Theodoretus" is a section mark (§) as printed. The reference marks g and h are not clearly visible in the text block; their position is taken from the margin notes beside the lines. "laudibꝰ" is the printed abbreviation with the -us sign. Printed "Thronique" and "Concludā" kept as printed.
